findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 436 lines and keeps the full Step 2.3-2.8 procedure inline while also requiring a complete read of references/wizard-flow.md, which repeats the same steps.
findings.fix: Keep the Step 0-4 route and the NEVER list in SKILL.md, and move Step 2.3 through 2.8 into the existing references, loaded only at the step that needs them.

findings.evidence: The file has 11 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger queries, but several negatives are unrelated (a unit test, a new SKILL.md, a GSD phase, a commit message) and several positives name the skill's own terms.
findings.fix: Replace the unrelated negatives with near-misses such as editing one lane by hand, changing only [runner] retry, running an already-configured review, and writing secrets.env, and add prompts that describe the job without naming lanes, config.toml or the wizard.

findings.evidence: The router-alias and stale-opencode cases use if and does-not wording, and both input files are notes rather than a config the procedure can run against.
findings.fix: Give those cases a real config fixture and assertions that check the printed alias label, the absence of a heuristic question, and the relayed warning line.

findings.evidence: The optional-key speech names artificialanalysis.ai and models.dev and tells the owner to edit ~/.config/ai-kit/secrets.env, with no source URL or date checked.
findings.fix: Read the catalog command's own --help in the run and relay that text, or attach the vendor's documentation URL and the date it was checked.

findings.evidence: The description covers setup, check-only and migration, but not the zero-price data-use confirmation or the per-role order and escalation questions.
findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set from the model catalog for the owner to pick, confirms data use before any zero-price lane, then asks each role's priority order, effort, escalation and opt-in flags, and writes the [lanes] table of ai-kit's config.toml. Writes the per-project ./.aikit/config.toml by default (always announces the exact path), asks before replacing an existing [lanes] table (local or global), and migrates an old review-spec.toml on first use. Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup, a lane order, or a check of reviewer availability, or when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers it because no lanes exist, even without naming config.toml. Supports --check-only (report availability, no writes), --local (force local write without asking), and --global (force the user ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ai-kit/config.toml directly). Not for running a review or an execute pass, editing [runner] or other tables, or writing secrets.env.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list gives reasons, but the write-risk, migration-backup and effort-refusal landmines sit only inside later steps.
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas section beside NEVER for the unconfirmed read-only probe, the keep-backup deletion default, and an effort refusal that writes nothing.

findings.evidence: The skill names itself a Process with Tool-level rigor, but the body is one long procedure rather than a compact process with checkpoints.
findings.fix: State the four phase checkpoints once and leave each phase's exact commands in the reference that phase already loads.

findings.evidence: Catalog discovery offers seed rows, a fixed web query, herdr and an owner-typed id as parallel sources.
findings.fix: Pick one default for a runtime with no listing and name the other sources as the escape hatch.

findings.evidence: Host tools restates that Bash means the shell, AskUserQuestion the question tool and Read the file reader.
findings.fix: Keep only the numbered plain-text fallback for a host with no question tool; move the tool-name gloss to references or record its removal.
